clue.text: Some crusty old clot in Major's cabinet

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written: the answer runs across the last letter of Major's and the start of cabinet

explanation.surface: A grumpy old fool sits in John Major's Cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'Major's cabinet'. 'Crusty old clot' sounds like an insult to a minister; read literally it is dried blood on a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the dry crust of clotted blood that forms over a healing wound.

clue.text: As may be seen by all, new Labour's started to be associated with pisspoor criminal

parts.words: As may be seen by all
parts.note: U is the British film certificate for a film anyone may watch

indicators.note: started means only the first letter of Labour's is taken

parts.note: first letter of Labour's
very bad, which is what awful means

explanation.surface: New Labour is publicly tied to a useless crook.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for universal viewing, so 'As may be seen by all' gives just that letter; 'started' takes L from Labour's.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawful means against the law, and criminal means the same as an adjective.

clue.text: Politician knight up on charge outside gets put away

indicators.note: outside means the charge word goes round the rest

parts.note: an ion is a charged particle
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the title is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title

explanation.surface: A knighted politician faces a charge and is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom, so the knight's title becomes RIS; 'outside' wraps the charge round everything. 'Charge' reads as a criminal charge, but it is an electrically charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone away is slang for jailing them, the sense of locking a prisoner up.

clue.text: Dirty film — a seventies thing — made by real bastard

parts.note: scum is a dirty film or layer on a liquid's surface
bag is slang from the sixties and seventies for one's thing, as in 'not my bag'

explanation.surface: A seedy seventies blue movie made by a nasty person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty film' suggests pornography, but it is a layer of grime.
explanation.definitionFit: Scumbag is coarse slang for a contemptible, despicable person.

clue.text: Minister appears when rising anger on left splits county council

indicators.note: splits means the pieces go into the middle of the council letters

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for county council

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the rising anger sits below the letter for left
rising in a down clue means the word for anger is read upwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A government minister emerges as a council row erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the anger word upwards as ERI, and 'on' places it under the left letter; 'splits' sends both between the two Cs. A minister is also a member of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a clergyman, so a cleric is the same churchman.

clue.text: Cover for members getting pissed on Sunday

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, as is pissed in British English

explanation.surface: Club members cover up after a boozy Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Members are limbs, here legs. In Britain pissed means drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting garment covering the legs, which are limbs or members of the body.

clue.text: Go round and castrate Blair's aide?

parts.note: to spin is to turn or go round
to doctor an animal is to neuter it

explanation.surface: An instruction to neuter Tony Blair's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Blair's aide as an example: Peter Mandelson and Alastair Campbell were famous New Labour spin doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a press adviser who presents news in the best light for a politician.

clue.text: Like top civil servants sparing us the uncomfortable details?

definitions.text: Like top civil servants sparing us the uncomfortable details?

parts.words: Like top civil servants sparing us the uncomfortable details?
parts.note: a famous phrase: Cabinet Secretary Sir Robert Armstrong said in the 1986 Spycatcher trial that a document had been sparing with the facts in just this way

explanation.surface: A dig at Whitehall mandarins who keep the awkward facts from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay: the clue describes the phrase. Sir Robert Armstrong, Britain's most senior civil servant, used it under cross-examination in Australia in 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means telling only part of the facts, the polite way of saying a senior official has misled you.

clue.text: More than one rogue is holding Major back

indicators.note: holding means the word is wraps round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the title is read the other way round

parts.note: John Major was the Prime Minister, PM for short

explanation.surface: A gang of villains are keeping the Prime Minister from going forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Major stands for his job, PM, which 'back' turns into MP; 'is' then holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are mischievous little devils, so the plural names several rascals or rogues.

clue.text: Somewhat blue appearance of a leading socialist?

parts.note: somewhat of the word blue: its opening letters only
an air is a manner or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A jibe that Labour's leader looks rather Tory blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative colour, so the surface says the Labour leader looks half Tory, a common jibe at Tony Blair in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair became leader of the Labour Party in 1994, so he was then Britain's leading socialist, the question mark admitting the irony.

clue.text: Ivory linked to this trafficker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: James Ivory's film partnership was ... Ivory, so this is the word joined to Ivory
second meaning: a trader or dealer in goods

explanation.walkthrough: Ivory looks like tusks smuggled by a poacher, but it is the film director's surname; his producer partner was Ismail Merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a dealer who buys and sells goods, and traffic is an old word for trade.

clue.text: Makes a balls-up by including 'eff-off' in talk

indicators.note: including means the word for talk takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: gas is idle chatter, as in to have a gas

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of eff are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written: the letters EFF

explanation.surface: Someone blunders by swearing in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff off' reads as a mild curse, but 'off' is the anagram signal turning eff into FFE, and 'including' sets that inside the word for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, so the verb in the third person means commits embarrassing mistakes.

clue.text: Marian's bent on litigation — an expensive habit

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Marian, its 's read as 'is' joining it to the anagram signal
a suit is a lawsuit, a case at law

explanation.surface: Marian is set on going to court, a costly addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' rearranges Marian into ARMANI, the Italian fashion label. 'Habit' is clothing, as in a riding habit, not an addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a costume or garment, and an Armani suit is a famously costly designer outfit.

clue.text: In circumstances, Tory hides old family member

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the words that follow
hides says the following words conceal the answer in their letters

parts.note: taken as written: the answer runs across the end of circumstances and the start of Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP covers up an embarrassing relative from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'hides' both say the answer is inside the words: it runs across the end of 'circumstances' and the start of 'Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear from earlier generations, someone from whom a person is descended.

clue.text: Sex appeal surrounding politician on left with a new — injection of hormones?

indicators.note: surrounding means the sex appeal word goes round the rest

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, from the 1920s It girl
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A sexy politician gets a hormone jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps the sex appeal word round everything after it. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a hormone pellet put under the skin is one kind of implant.
explanation.definitionFit: An implant is something inserted into the body, such as a slow-release hormone pellet.

clue.text: Bill's a solid figure constraining Tory leader

indicators.note: constraining means the figure holds the other letter within it

parts.note: a statue is a figure carved or cast in solid stone or bronze

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Tory

parts.note: first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A Parliamentary bill is compared to a statue boxing in the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes T from Tory, and 'constraining' has STATUE hold it. Read 'Bill's' as 'Bill is': the definition is the bill, and the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a law passed by Parliament, which is what a bill becomes once it is enacted.

clue.text: See 8
Piss-artists puckering pert lips

indicators.note: puckering means screwing up or wrinkling, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drunks purse their cheeky lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puckering' rearranges the letters of 'pert lips'. A piss-artist is British slang for a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipplers are habitual drinkers, the same sense as the slang for confirmed boozers.

clue.text: Spotting Nige madly hugging agent

indicators.note: hugging means the jumbled letters wrap round the agent
madly means wildly, so the letters of Nige are rearranged

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A spotter sees Nige wildly embracing a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' scrambles Nige into EING, and 'hugging' has it split round the agent, one letter at the front and three behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, so the present participle means seeing or noticing.

clue.text: Tits such as the likes of Black Rod

definitions.meaning: second meaning: people who knock; Black Rod knocks three times on the Commons door at the State Opening of Parliament

explanation.walkthrough: Tits could be birds, but here they are breasts. Black Rod is the House of Lords officer whose door-knocking summons MPs to hear the Queen's Speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both crude slang for breasts and a plain noun for anyone who raps on a door.

clue.text: Just the place for brats at work?

definitions.text: Just the place for brats at work?

parts.words: Just the place for brats at work?
parts.note: a nursery where parents leave small children during the working day

explanation.walkthrough: The brats are not at work themselves: the place is for the children of parents who are working.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery, often at a workplace, where infants are minded while their parents work.

clue.text: Tebbit, having lost the race — no good, on the decline

indicators.note: the race is the TT, and those two letters are Tebbit's first and last, so losing them leaves only the middle

parts.note: Norman Tebbit, Conservative politician; taken as written

explanation.surface: Norman Tebbit, out of the running, is useless and fading.
explanation.walkthrough: The race is the TT, the Isle of Man motorbike race; Tebbit's two Ts are its first and last letters, so 'having lost the race' leaves EBBI. Norman Tebbit was a combative Thatcher-era Tory minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing describes a tide going out, and so anything waning or dwindling.

clue.text: Our monarch no longer has one — it's provided by parliamentarian in a republic

definitions.text: Our monarch no longer has one

indicators.note: in means the parliamentarian sits inside the republic's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name of the Republic of Ireland
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The Queen has lost something that a politician in a republic can provide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the parliamentarian inside the Irish name for Ireland. The definition is a description: Britain's monarch once ruled an empire but no longer does.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Empire was dismantled after the Second World War, so the Crown no longer rules vast overseas dominions.

clue.text: Meeting of politicians gives you erection

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gathering of elected representatives
second meaning: the putting together of parts, as in building a flat-pack wardrobe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Erection' tempts a rude reading, but it is the act of erecting, putting something together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a body of lawmakers and the construction of a thing from its parts.

clue.text: What Brenda does, left to penetrate foreign ways

indicators.note: to penetrate means the letter for left goes into the streets

parts.note: rues are streets in French, so foreign roads or ways

explanation.surface: The Queen's doings, with a leftist breaking into foreign ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to penetrate' puts L inside RUES. Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch reigns over a country, and to rule is to govern, which is the sovereign's job.

clue.text: Southern support for religious arse makes you puke

parts.note: a pew is a church bench that supports a churchgoer's backside

explanation.surface: A pious backside in the south makes someone sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Arse is the British form of ass, a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, and puke is slang for vomiting.

clue.text: See 8
Santer involved in right-on backing for Eurotrain in its early days?

indicators.note: backing means the word on is turned round to run the other way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Jacques Santer, then President of the European Commission; taken as written

explanation.surface: The EU chief backs a cross-Channel rail scheme in its earliest stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ON into NO; 'involved' mixes SANTER with RT into NSTARTER. The Channel Tunnel train service was long delayed, so the question mark offers it as an example of a doomed project.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-starter is a plan or idea with no chance of success, a fair jibe at a long-delayed rail project.
